title: Singapore Work Visa Requirements 2026: EP & S Pass Guide
metaDescription: Singapore work visa requirements 2026: Employment Pass from S$5,600, S Pass from S$3,300, the COMPASS points test, quotas and how employers apply.
headline: Singapore Work Visa Requirements 2026: Full Guide

sections.title: Employment Pass and the COMPASS test
sections.content:
The Employment Pass (EP) is Singapore's main work pass for foreign professionals, managers, executives and specialists. In 2026 the minimum qualifying salary is S$5,600 a month for most sectors and about S$6,200 for financial services, rising with age to S$10,700, or about S$12,000 in finance, for candidates aged 45 and above.

Since September 2023 every EP application is also scored under COMPASS, the Complementarity Assessment Framework, across six criteria including salary, qualifications, diversity and support for local employment. Applicants need at least 40 points to qualify, unless exempt. From 1 January 2027 the EP floor rises to S$6,000 for most sectors and S$6,600 for financial services for new applications.

sections.title: S Pass: mid-skilled workers, quotas and levy
sections.content:
The S Pass covers mid-skilled technicians, associate professionals and specialists who do not meet EP criteria on salary or qualifications. It requires a relevant diploma or degree, and in 2026 the minimum salary is S$3,300 a month for most sectors, rising with age to about S$5,000 at 45 and above. From 1 January 2027 the floor rises to S$3,600, or S$4,000 for financial services.

Employers face a quota: S Pass holders cannot exceed 10% of the workforce in services or 15% in manufacturing, and the employer pays a foreign worker levy of S$650 a month per S Pass holder, a single rate in force since 1 September 2025. S Pass holders can bring dependants only if they earn at least S$6,000 a month.

sections.title: Work Permits and other passes
sections.content:
The Work Permit covers lower-skilled workers in sectors such as construction, manufacturing, marine shipyard, process and services, with no minimum qualifying salary but strict quotas, levies and source-country rules. Other passes include the ONE Pass for top talent earning at least S$30,000 a month, the Personalised Employment Pass for high earners, and EntrePass for entrepreneurs.

Singapore does not issue a generic work visa: every foreign employee needs a work pass sponsored by a registered Singapore employer or an Employer of Record. The sponsoring employer applies through the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) portal, and passes are usually issued for up to two years at first, then renewable.

sections.title: How employers apply: the Fair Consideration Framework
sections.content:
Before hiring a foreign candidate, most employers must advertise the role on MyCareersFuture for at least 14 days under the Fair Consideration Framework, unless an exemption applies, such as companies with fewer than 10 employees, jobs paying S$22,500 a month or more, or intra-corporate transferees.

Singapore's labour market was tight in 2026, with overall unemployment at 1.9% in June 2026 and 68,600 job vacancies, or 1.48 vacancies per unemployed person. EP holders can bring dependants on a Dependant's Pass, and the whole family can use Singapore's public healthcare and schooling systems while the pass remains valid.

faqs.q: What is the minimum salary for a Singapore Employment Pass in 2026?
faqs.a: The Employment Pass minimum qualifying salary in 2026 is S$5,600 a month for most sectors and about S$6,200 for financial services, rising with age to S$10,700 or about S$12,000 in finance at age 45 and above. From 1 January 2027 the floor rises to S$6,000 and S$6,600 for new applications. Applicants must also score at least 40 points under COMPASS.

faqs.q: What is the S Pass minimum salary in 2026?
faqs.a: The S Pass minimum qualifying salary in 2026 is S$3,300 a month for most sectors, rising with age to S$5,000 at 45 and above, with higher figures for financial services. From 1 January 2027 the floor rises to S$3,600, or S$4,000 in finance. Employers must respect the quota and pay a levy of S$650 a month per S Pass holder.

faqs.q: What is COMPASS in Singapore work passes?
faqs.a: COMPASS is the Complementarity Assessment Framework, a points system the Ministry of Manpower has applied to Employment Pass applications since September 2023. It scores candidates across six criteria, including salary relative to local norms, qualifications, workforce diversity and support for local employment. Applicants need at least 40 points to qualify for an EP.

faqs.q: Can I bring my family to Singapore on a work pass?
faqs.a: Employment Pass holders can bring a spouse and children on a Dependant's Pass, with no minimum salary beyond the EP threshold itself. S Pass holders can bring dependants only if they earn at least S$6,000 a month. Work Permit holders generally cannot bring dependants, so the pass type matters as much as the salary.
